A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniDB research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniDB image-restoration experiments, penalty-coefficient ablations and qualitative outputs in Section 5 and Appendix E, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds CelebA-HQ thick-mask inpainting results in Appendix C, Table 6.

M1.justification: The optimal controller, finite-penalty construction, training loss, sampling procedure and UniDB-GOU/VE/VP variants are retained. Algorithms 1–2 move into the main text. Corrected score expressions agree with derivations already present in v1 and do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v4 adds thick-mask CelebA-HQ inpainting in Table 6, extending the input-corruption scenarios beyond the retained thin-mask evaluation. DIV2K, Rain100H, CelebA-HQ and FFHQ coverage otherwise remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in corresponding Tables 1–5 is unchanged. New Table 6 reuses DDRM, IR-SDE, printed as IRSDE, and GOUB; it introduces no new comparison method or replacement within a retained comparison.

E3.justification: Table 6 adds a thick-mask evaluation condition without replacing the existing 100-thin-mask experiment. Existing splits, metrics, training budget and 100 sampling steps remain unchanged. The new masks' generation procedure and count are not specified.

E4.justification: The added thick-mask evaluation provides a limited check under more extensive missing-image regions. The qualitative deraining comparison also gains a statue example with GOUB comparison in v4 Figure 3. The penalty-coefficient ablation and terminal-distance analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The shaded region in the terminal-distance plot marks the selected penalty range, not statistical uncertainty, in both versions.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results. New Table 6 reports UniDB-GOU versus GOUB on thick-mask inpainting: PSNR 23.02 versus 22.59, LPIPS 0.0884 versus 0.0917 and FID 7.46 versus 8.49, but slightly lower SSIM, 0.8571 versus 0.8573. These are additional results under a different masking condition.

T1.justification: v4 adds expectations to the stochastic objectives in Equations (9) and (11) and restores missing logarithms in the score expressions in Equations (15)–(16) and Sections 4.3/A.5. These are limited mathematical corrections; the theorem statements and principal proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: SOC unification of diffusion bridges, Doob's h-transform as the infinite-penalty case, minimal implementation changes and improved restoration detail. The additional experiment does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 expands the interpretation of finite penalties, explicitly connecting reduced control effort and small endpoint mismatches to smoother trajectories and more natural images. v1 gives a shorter cost-versus-quality explanation. The computationally intensive sampling limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix D and v4 Appendix B disclose the same network, noise schedule, optimizer, training budget, dataset splits, hardware and approximate training time. The code-access information is unchanged. Relocated pseudocode and added comparison highlighting do not provide a new UniDB implementation procedure.

R1.justification: The reference to Mania, Tu and Recht on certainty equivalence is removed. Most other reference changes update metadata for the same works. The Schrödinger-bridge discussion moves from v1 Appendix C into Section 2, retaining its positioning rather than introducing a new research comparison.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact. Existing pseudocode and related-work material move into the main text, local explanations and cross-references are revised, and authorship and acknowledgments are updated. The running title is unfortunately replaced by the template text 'Submission and Formatting Instructions for ICML 2025'.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is rebuilt from a restoration montage into a diffusion/SOC schematic. The main deraining/inpainting grid is transposed and expanded, algorithms move into the main text with revised highlighting, Table 6 is added, and several appendix image grids gain explicit input/output labels. Together these substantially revise the visual explanation and organization.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful evidence beyond v1's thin-mask evaluation, corrects expected-cost and log-score expressions, and improves visual explanation and labeling. The gains are limited because the core method and existing numerical evidence remain unchanged, while the new mask protocol is underspecified. The erroneous template running header also reduces presentation polish, but does not outweigh these improvements.
